nullsens.ar_delta_p05.spec: rise in the null's fifth percentile from i.i.d. to AR(1)=0.6, both averaged over 20 independent seeds -- the departure that does move the benchmark, in the direction that makes the i.i.d. comparison ANTI-conservative for a lower-tail claim rather than conservative

nullsens.p05_ar06.spec: fifth percentile under AR(1)=0.6 serial dependence in every model's loss, averaged over 20 independent seeds. Serial dependence DOES raise the null, which matters for §5.4's lower-tail claims: a higher null puts an observed low value further into the tail, so the i.i.d. benchmark flags FEWER cells as unusual than a realistic one would

nullsens.p05_iid.spec: fifth percentile of winner_stability under the i.i.d. exchangeable null at K=6, T=30, averaged over 20 independent seeds (8000 effective replications). This is the same construction as the benchmark the paper ships for §5.4, run at this sweep's own T=30 rather than §5.4's T=32; the two p05 figures agree to 3 dp

nullsens.p05_rho05.spec: the same fifth percentile when half the loss variance is a shock COMMON to every model, averaged over 20 independent seeds

nullsens.p05_rho08.spec: the same fifth percentile at eighty percent common variance, averaged over 20 independent seeds. Equal (within seed noise) to the rho=0.5 value because winner_stability counts argmin preservation and argmin is invariant to a shift applied to every model in a period -- the statistic cannot see the common component

nullsens.rho_delta_p05.spec: absolute change in the null's fifth percentile between eighty and fifty percent common variance, both averaged over 20 independent seeds. Emitted because the INVARIANCE is the finding: a common shock across models might be expected to raise the null, but doubling the correlation moves it by only this much
